Topics · Is the Quran from God?

Are the Quran's "scientific miracles" real?

This app does not use them: many rest on strained readings, and the book does not claim to teach science.

Part 1 of 3

﴿يَسْـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلْأَهِلَّةِ ۖ قُلْ هِىَ مَوَٰقِيتُ لِلنَّاسِ وَٱلْحَجِّ ۗ وَلَيْسَ ٱلْبِرُّ بِأَن تَأْتُوا۟ ٱلْبُيُوتَ مِن ظُهُورِهَا وَلَـٰكِنَّ ٱلْبِرَّ مَنِ ٱتَّقَىٰ ۗ وَأْتُوا۟ ٱلْبُيُوتَ مِنْ أَبْوَٰبِهَا ۚ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

They ask you, [O Muḥammad], about the crescent moons. Say, "They are measurements of time for the people and for ḥajj [pilgrimage]." And it is not righteousness to enter houses from the back, but righteousness is [in] one who fears Allāh. And enter houses from their doors. And fear Allāh that you may succeed.

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:189

Translation

God said, “Let there be lights in the expanse of the sky to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs to mark seasons, days, and years;

Original · Hebrew

וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֗ים יְהִ֤י מְאֹרֹת֙ בִּרְקִ֣יעַ הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם לְהַבְדִּ֕יל בֵּ֥ין הַיּ֖וֹם וּבֵ֣ין הַלָּ֑יְלָה וְהָי֤וּ לְאֹתֹת֙ וּלְמ֣וֹעֲדִ֔ים וּלְיָמִ֖ים וְשָׁנִֽים׃

the Torah (Genesis) · 1:14

World English Bible

If you were raised on these claims and then checked them, you were right to check. Many do not survive close reading, and this app does not use them. Here is why that costs the Quran nothing. It does not present itself as a science text. When people asked about the new moons, the reply was not about astronomy. It told them what the moon is for: marking time. Most of its signs ask people to reflect on what they already see.

A question for you

What did these claims do for you?

If you sayThey steadied my faith for a while, then failed me.
ThenMany tell this story. An overpromise does more harm than good, which is why it is dropped here.
If you sayI still think some are strong.
ThenYou may weigh each claim by itself. The next part gives a standard for that.
If you sayI never believed them.
ThenThen you do not need this part, and nothing here relies on it.

Part 2 of 3

﴿وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْإِنسَـٰنَ مِن سُلَـٰلَةٍ مِّن طِينٍ١٢ ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَـٰهُ نُطْفَةً فِى قَرَارٍ مَّكِينٍ١٣ ثُمَّ خَلَقْنَا ٱلنُّطْفَةَ عَلَقَةً فَخَلَقْنَا ٱلْعَلَقَةَ مُضْغَةً فَخَلَقْنَا ٱلْمُضْغَةَ عِظَـٰمًا فَكَسَوْنَا ٱلْعِظَـٰمَ لَحْمًا ثُمَّ أَنشَأْنَـٰهُ خَلْقًا ءَاخَرَ ۚ فَتَبَارَكَ ٱللَّهُ أَحْسَنُ ٱلْخَـٰلِقِينَ١٤﴾

Original · Hebrew

יָדֶ֣יךָ עִ֭צְּבוּנִי וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֑וּנִי יַ֥חַד סָ֝בִ֗יב וַֽתְּבַלְּעֵֽנִי׃ זְכָר־נָ֭א כִּי־כַחֹ֣מֶר עֲשִׂיתָ֑נִי וְֽאֶל־עָפָ֥ר תְּשִׁיבֵֽנִי׃ הֲלֹ֣א כֶ֭חָלָב תַּתִּיכֵ֑נִי וְ֝כַגְּבִנָּ֗ה תַּקְפִּיאֵֽנִי׃ ע֣וֹר וּ֭בָשָׂר תַּלְבִּישֵׁ֑נִי וּֽבַעֲצָמ֥וֹת וְ֝גִידִ֗ים תְּסֹכְכֵֽנִי׃ חַיִּ֣ים וָ֭חֶסֶד עָשִׂ֣יתָ עִמָּדִ֑י וּ֝פְקֻדָּתְךָ֗ שָֽׁמְרָ֥ה רוּחִֽי׃

Job · 10:8-12

World English Bible

﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓا۟ أَنَّ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ كَانَتَا رَتْقًا فَفَتَقْنَـٰهُمَا ۖ وَجَعَلْنَا مِنَ ٱلْمَآءِ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ حَىٍّ ۖ أَفَلَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Have those who disbelieved not considered that the heavens and the earth were a joined entity, and then We separated them and made from water every living thing? Then will they not believe?

Quran · Al-Anbiya 21:30

Take the two most famous cases. The stages of the embryo in the first passage do describe a sequence, but similar descriptions existed in Greek medicine centuries earlier, and the words themselves are general. The second passage, on the heavens and earth being joined, is read as the Big Bang, but classical readers took it otherwise, and it fits many pictures. A test is not 'can a modern idea be found here?' Almost anything can be found if you look hard enough.

A question for you

Which test seems most important for a claim like this?

If you sayWas it understood before the discovery?
ThenThat is a strong test, and it removes many claims.
If you sayWas the idea available then?
ThenThat takes real historical knowledge, not impressions, in both directions.
If you sayDoes it treat the hard verses by the same rule?
ThenThat is the test of fairness, and it comes next.

Part 3 of 3

﴿حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا بَلَغَ مَغْرِبَ ٱلشَّمْسِ وَجَدَهَا تَغْرُبُ فِى عَيْنٍ حَمِئَةٍ وَوَجَدَ عِندَهَا قَوْمًا ۗ قُلْنَا يَـٰذَا ٱلْقَرْنَيْنِ إِمَّآ أَن تُعَذِّبَ وَإِمَّآ أَن تَتَّخِذَ فِيهِمْ حُسْنًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

Until, when he reached the setting of the sun [i.e., the west], he found it [as if] setting in a body of dark water,[795] and he found near it a people. We [i.e., Allāh] said, "O Dhul-Qarnayn, either you punish [them] or else adopt among them [a way of] goodness."

Translator's notes

[795] Another meaning is "a body of hot water."

Quran · Al-Kahf 18:86

﴿وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن رَّسُولٍ إِلَّا بِلِسَانِ قَوْمِهِۦ لِيُبَيِّنَ لَهُمْ ۖ فَيُضِلُّ ٱللَّهُ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَهْدِى مَن يَشَآءُ ۚ وَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And We did not send any messenger except [speaking] in the language of his people to state clearly for them, and Allāh sends astray [thereby] whom He wills[649] and guides whom He wills. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.

Translator's notes

[649] i.e., those who refuse His guidance.

Quran · Ibrahim 14:4

Fairness cuts both ways. Critics point to a sun setting in a muddy spring. The sentence says he found it so: it can be read as how the sight looked to a traveller. A critic will call that convenient. So use one rule for both sides: do not press a verse to say more than it says, for or against. The second passage says every messenger spoke in his people's tongue. A book in a people's tongue speaks of the world in words they could understand.

A question for you

What do you need from a book claiming to be from God, on matters of nature?

If you sayThat it is never wrong on any reading.
ThenThat is a serious standard. The Quran is true; what can err is a human reading of it, and this app does not defend every reading.
If you sayThat this is not its subject at all.
ThenThat is close to what the book says of itself. The critic still asks about what it says in passing.
If you sayI don't know yet.
ThenThat is a fair answer, and it can be set before looking at any claim.
